The Apollo program landed twelve astronauts on the Moon between 1969 and 1972.
Apollo 11 was the first crewed landing: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin touched
down in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20, 1969, while Michael Collins remained
in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia.

The program's budget peaked at roughly 4 percent of the United States federal
budget. Saturn V, the launch vehicle used for the missions, remains the most
powerful rocket ever flown successfully, standing 111 metres tall.

Later missions added the Lunar Roving Vehicle, extending surface exploration
range from hundreds of metres to tens of kilometres. Apollo 17 closed the
program in December 1972 with astronaut-geologist Harrison Schmitt.
